bioghist.head: Biographical/Historical Information
bioghist.p: The Real Estate Board was established in 1924 to regulate businesses and individuals representing others in real property transactions, including condominiums, cooperatives, and time-shares. The Board issues licenses to persons, partnerships, associations or corporations to act as real estate brokers or real estate salesmen or to advertise or assume to act as such real estate brokers or real estate salesmen and to promulgate regulations for education requirements for licensure and relicensure. An adjunct responsibility allows the Board to investigate housing discrimination under the aegis of the Federal Fair Housing Act. The Dept. of Professional and Occupational Regulation provides administrative support to the board.

odd.p: These records are part of the Virginia Dept. of Professional and Occupational Regulation record group (RG 17)

Electronic records in this collection are read-only and are only available in the Archives Research Room at the Library of Virginia. A file list is available through the online catalog entry and the link below in the finding aid. Copies are free of charge and may be requested while using the collection in-house. Copies may also be requested by contacting Archives Reference Services. Processing will take from 4-8 weeks.

accessrestrict.p: Meeting attachments must be reviewed for personal information and redacted prior to being served.

scopecontent.p: Minutes and related attachments documenting the meetings, activities, discussions, policy decisions, and recommendations of the Virginia Real Estate Board. Includes official board minutes. Includes official board minutes, as well as draft minutes, committee meeting minutes, agendas and other meeting materials. May also include informal fact finding hearing minutes, agreements, Fair Housing Committee minutes, committee reports, correspondence, guideines, legislation, regulations and reports.
Topics may include alternative dispute resolutions, budgets, common interest community, fair housing, funds, and licensing fees.

Electronic records often contain board meeting packets with various attachments and draft minutes, while paper records often include minutes only. There may be some duplication between paper and electronic records. For transfers prior to 2012, records of individual boards were accessioned separately. After this, transfers of records (records starting in 2008) included all boards, which were accessioned under one accession number. There is a separate finding aid for the later transfers (link to finding aid below).

Board minutes and board meeting packets, 2002-2004, are in electronic format (9.89 mb, 9 folders, 22 files; format: pdf). Includes agendas, draft minutes, Fair Housing Committee minutes, agreements, correspondence, legislative summaries, regulations, and reports. For file inventory for this accession, see: Inventory (44800).

Board minutes and board meeting packets, 2006 (44990), are in electronice format (5.39 mb, 15 files, 12 folders; format: doc, pdf). Includes agendas, draft minutes, agreements, correspondence, legislatiion, and reports and studies on issues relating to Common Interest Communities. For file inventory for this accession, see: Inventory (44989).

Board minutes and board meeting packets, 2006 (44990), are in electronice format (3.45 mb, 37 files, 15 folders; format: doc, pdf). Includes agendas, draft minutes, agreements, committee reports, correspondence, regulations, and records related to Common Interest Communties. For file inventory for this accession, see: Inventory (44990).

Minutes, 2008, are in electronic format. Minutes, 2009-2010, are in paper format. Folders are included in a box with minutes from other DPOR boards. For guide for this accession, see: Finding aid (51228).

Minutes, 2014-2015 are in electronic format. Minutes, 2011-2013, are in paper format. Folders are included in a box with minutes from other DPOR boards. For guide for this accession, see: Finding aid (51966).
